section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic reporting from the American Embassy in Tokyo covering late November 1937 through December 1937, consisting of the latter portion of the November monthly political report and the complete December 1937 monthly report (transmitted under Despatch No. 2735). Major international developments documented include the Japanese military advance and capture of Nanking, the establishment of Japanese-sponsored puppet régimes across occupied China, the sinking of the U.S.S. Panay and artillery attacks on H.M.S. Ladybird and Bee on the Yangtze River, and subsequent diplomatic representations, apologies, and settlements. The reports also detail negotiations over the Chinese Maritime Customs administration at Shanghai, Japan's recognition of the Franco government in Spain, Italy's accession to the Anti-Comintern Pact, Soviet-Japanese border and fisheries tensions, and domestic Japanese wartime mobilization, including the creation of Imperial General Headquarters and the expansion of economic controls.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of the American Embassy in Tokyo's monthly political report for November 1937, reviewing international relations, domestic politics, and economic conditions, with annex lists of despatches and telegrams sent during the month.
subfiles.summary: This concluding section of the November 1937 report documents Japanese military operations and friction with third powers over the International Settlement and Chinese Maritime Customs administration in Shanghai, rising anti-British agitation in Japan, and the bilateral treaty between Japan and Manchukuo abolishing Japanese extraterritorial rights. It records Italy's accession to the Anti-Comintern Pact and its de jure recognition of Manchukuo, Soviet-Japanese friction over border incidents and the deportation of Korean residents from the Maritime Province, and Japan's refusal to attend the Nine Power Treaty Conference in Brussels. Internal affairs highlight the establishment of Imperial General Headquarters, the approval of the draft 1938-1939 budget, state control legislation for the electric power and coal industries, and foreign trade statistics, concluding with comprehensive indexes of Embassy despatches (Nos. 2648–2681) and telegrams (Nos. 506–583) transmitted to the Department during November 1937.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of November, 1937

subfiles.about: Embassy Despatch No. 2735 transmitting the comprehensive monthly report on political, international, military, and economic conditions in Japan during December 1937.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2735 transmits the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for December 1937, dominated by the December 12 Japanese aerial sinking of the U.S.S. Panay and Standard Oil tankers above Nanking and the simultaneous artillery shelling of British gunboats H.M.S. Ladybird and Bee at Wuhu, detailing subsequent American and British protests, Japanese admissions of responsibility, official apologies, and promises of indemnification. The report chronicles the capture of Nanking, operations in Shantung, and the creation of Japanese-sponsored autonomous administrations, including the Provisional Government of China at Peiping, alongside diplomatic friction concerning the Shanghai Maritime Customs, American and French extraterritorial rights in Manchuria, and Japanese salmon fishing in Alaskan waters. It further documents Japan's formal recognition of the Franco government in Spain, the extension of the Soviet-Japanese fisheries agreement, domestic political consolidation under new Home Minister Admiral Suetsugu, mass arrests of left-wing figures, opening of the 73rd Diet session, bond issuances, and tightened foreign exchange controls, concluding with a list of outgoing telegrams (Nos. 584–611) sent during December.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2735: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of December, 1937
